content.body:
Probably the most famous tank of WW2, the Tiger had a long development. From an original design for a modest 33 ton breakthrough tank, it ballooned to a 57-ton behemoth after the humbling first encounters with the Russian T34. Despite its heavy armor and superb gun, the Tigers initial performance in combat was unimpressive, with it suffering extensively from mechanical breakdown due to a rushed deployment. After the teething problems were largely solved, the Tiger earned its fearsome reputation at the hands of audacious commanders like Michael Wittman, his skilled crew credited with knocking out 141 tanks and 132 AT guns.
Control Variations:
The Tiger is an outstanding vehicle, close to undefeatable by any other tank in the game if used properly. The exceptionally good gun means that anytime you engage a target at less than 500m, you are handing them a significant chance they would not otherwise ever have, and counteracting your own strengths which is foolish. Keep your very thick frontal aspect armour in mind at all times - facing an enemy will make you almost invulnerable to most except the very best Allied AT guns, basically those 76mm or more in caliber or the high velocity 6 pounder if he gets close enough to you.
But beware of aircraft - you are a high value target that enemy pilots will be searching contantly for. The Tigers massive gun means a relatively slow turret speed, but this also means that the Tiger is a particularly effective tank for multicrewing if you follow the famous Wittmans example, who innovated the clever and expedient maneuver of assisted slewing, where the driver would also spin the tank as hard as possible while the slower turret turned in the same direction, giving the tank an effective turret slew rate much higher than available by simply traversing the gun - probably worth practicing with a regular multicrew buddy.
